results.summary_before: DreiMann implements a dice-based party game where two button presses simulate rolling two dice and the result is shown on a seven-segment display. The display encodes doubles as the number 1-6, a 1-and-2 combination as all segments lit, a single 3 as the three horizontal lines, and any other combination as the middle line only. It needs two push buttons on inputs 0 and 1, an optional switch on input 2 to select common anode or common cathode, and a seven-segment display wired to the eight outputs. The design is a straightforward Verilog game with no reported silicon results and is intended to be played socially rather than tested automatically.

results.summary_before: This Verilog project is a modified VGA checker pattern generator that outputs standard VGA signals. It is based on the Tiny Tapeout VGA template, with changes made to reverse the direction and alter the default colors. To use it, one connects the outputs to a VGA display and observes the generated graphics. The project is notable for being a simple template derivative intended for experimentation with VGA output on Tiny Tapeout.

results.summary_before: This is a silicon art project that places a pixel pig artwork and canary token text directly on the metal layers of the chip using a custom GDS workflow. The design includes a decorative border and density fill to meet metal coverage requirements, and all digital outputs are tied to ground. The art is visible under an optical microscope after fabrication, and no external hardware is required. The project is notable for being purely decorative and for demonstrating the custom GDS capabilities of the Tiny Tapeout IHP process.

add.reason: The design is explicitly a CA-CFAR radar target detector processing radar samples.

results.notes: Swapped sensor-interface for radar: the input is a radar sample bus and the design is a radar detector.
results.summary_before: CFAR Radar Detector is a low-area cell-averaging constant false alarm rate accelerator that estimates background noise from a sliding window of training cells around a cell under test. Radar amplitude samples arrive on the 8-bit input bus, and a detection is asserted when the cell under test exceeds twice the averaged noise, with a buzzer alert output. It is fully digital and needs no external hardware, though outputs could drive a buzzer, LED, or radar front end. It is verified in Icarus Verilog with a testbench and an example input sequence containing a strong reflection.

results.summary_before: This project is a small demoscene-style VGA generator that produces a 640x480 @ 60Hz video signal with an animated XOR background and a central logo inspired by the Tiny Tapeout mark. The image is computed entirely in hardware using combinational logic, without a frame buffer or external memory. Two input pins allow inverting colors and freezing the logo at the center. It requires a VGA PMOD for video output and is tested by connecting it to a Tiny Tapeout demo board.
